question: Decompose the 15.1% of netted FY2024 DAF grants that no itemised panel Schedule I line reaches (itemising panel coverage 84.9%): quantify Schedule F foreign grants, sub-$5,000 non-itemised grants (Part IX line 1 less Schedule I total), non-itemising sponsors (BofA CGF $1.04bn and RCF $0.72bn raw FY2024 DAF grants) and the DAF-weighting haircut, so the residual 1/0.849 scaling can be replaced or bounded
conclusion_affected: Whether the directly measured pooled share (7.3% of 1h, 12.1% of 1h-1d-1e) or the residual-scaled one (8.7% / 14.2%) is the better all-sponsor figure
rationale: The direct estimate is a floor for the 15.1% the panel's itemised lines do not reach; the residual scaling assumes that money reaches frame recipients in the measured proportions, which foreign grants and sub-$5,000 gifts do not

question: Replace the default DAF weight of 1 for the 226 sponsor-years with no DAF share (111 community foundations, 74 single-issue charities, 27 universities and hospitals, $0.78bn of Schedule I) using Schedule D Part I grants from their own returns, re-read from the mirror
conclusion_affected: Numerator purity for single-issue and university sponsors (e.g. Vanderbilt University FY2023 $61m of Schedule I)
rationale: A weight of 0 for these sponsor-years moves the expanded-frame pooled share only from 7.35% to 7.31%, so this is cleanup rather than a conclusion risk

question: Exclude non-panel DAF sponsors and pass-through intermediaries from the expanded frame with a rule rather than a name regex: Schedule D Part I present on the recipient's own FY2023-24 return, or Schedule I outbound grants above 50% of expenses; JFNA is the largest single non-top-50 recipient in the sample ($90.5m) and UJA-Federation still escapes the regex
conclusion_affected: Pooled shares in the expanded frame (7.3% of 1h; 7.0% with the leaked-sponsor regex)
rationale: Non-top-50 sponsors give relatively more to federations and other re-granters, so the intermediary question now matters for the non-top-50 part too

question: Re-estimate the size and sector cuts in the new-only frame with a larger supplementary sample (70,008 EINs that receive only non-top-50 grants; 1,272 sampled, 1,094 in scope): 80 per stratum in the <$1m and $1-5m bands where community-foundation money concentrates
conclusion_affected: Small-recipient medians and the share of recipients at or above 20% in the expanded frame
rationale: The new-only pooled share (1.8% of 1h) rests on a weighted population of 44,698 with wide intervals (1.1-3.0%)
